options: A visual diagram of every role in the system
A relationship between a role and a set of conditions, configured in Manage Role Provisioning Rules
A list of passwords for every user
A synonym for a data access set
questions.explain: A role mapping defines the conditions (such as job and business unit) under which a role is automatically or self-requestable, and it is configured through Manage Role Provisioning Rules.

questions.q: Which provisioning method grants a role automatically the moment a matching assignment is created, with no human action required?
options: Manual provisioning
Self-request
Autoprovisioning
Emergency provisioning
questions.explain: Autoprovisioning automatically grants a role when a user's assignment matches all the conditions of a role mapping that has the Autoprovision option selected.

questions.q: A role mapping has the Self-requestable option selected. What does that allow?
options: Any user whose assignment matches the mapping's conditions can request that role themselves, usually subject to approval
Only administrators can ever assign that role
The role becomes available to every user in the company with no conditions
The role is automatically removed from all existing users
questions.explain: Self-requestable roles can be requested by any matching user, typically going through an approval workflow (covered in Lesson 16).

questions.q: Why can't a purely manual user account, such as one created for an external auditor with no worker record, receive a role through autoprovisioning?
options: Autoprovisioning is reserved for abstract roles only
External auditors are never allowed any access
Autoprovisioning does not exist in Oracle Fusion
Autoprovisioned roles can only be added to users who have associated worker information
questions.explain: Autoprovisioning depends on a worker assignment matching the role mapping's conditions, so it requires the user to have an associated worker record.

questions.q: What is the practical consequence of poorly designed role mappings during an implementation?
options: No consequence, since provisioning rules never affect real access
The Security Console becomes permanently locked
Either over-provisioning (users getting access they shouldn't have) or under-provisioning (manual fix-ups needed for every new hire)
All existing users automatically lose their current roles
questions.explain: Poorly designed role mappings lead to either granting too much access automatically (a segregation-of-duties risk) or too little (requiring manual correction for every new hire).
